            items:
              maxLength: 250

            type: array
        - description: A tag ID to exclude. Accepts a single tag ID or multiple tag IDs. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag IDs are excluded.

          required: false
          schema:
            default: []
            description: Tag IDs associated with this dashboard.
            items:
              maxLength: 250
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
        - description: A tag name to include. Accepts a single tag name or multiple tag names. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag names are included. If the same name is shared by multiple tags, items matching any of those tags are included.

content.text:
The dashboard and the alert rule both exist, and the rule is enabled. I haven't opened the dashboard to check how it renders. I also didn't test whether the rule fires, because a rule that only appears on the first scheduled run wasn't something I could check from here.

**Data**: The `kibana_sample_data_logs` data view has `timestamp`, `bytes`, `clientip`, `response` (a string, with a `.keyword` subfield), `extension`, `geo.*`, `machine.os`, `request`, `url`, `agent` and `referer`.

**Dashboard**: "EFF-5ffa4650 Web logs overview" (id `96b22d87-41df-40ee-84fe-76a166339e36`) has four panels and defaults to the last 7 days:
- Total requests (count)
- Average bytes
- Unique clients (distinct `clientip`)
- Requests over time (line chart)

**Rule**: "EFF-5ffa4650 5xx spike" (id `dc233291-c6db-4e87-96b6-331b349470c1`) is an Elasticsearch query rule. It runs every minute over the last 5 minutes. It counts documents where `response.keyword` matches `5[0-9][0-9]` and fires when the count is above 10. It has no actions attached, so a firing only shows up in Kibana and doesn't notify anyone.

My first dashboard attempts were rejected by the API; I fixed the line chart's data source and the dashboard was created on the next try.
